newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU environment ministers to focus on small firms.
newsitem.headline: EU environment ministers to focus on small firms.

text.p: European Union environment ministers are due to meet this weekend to address the problem of getting the EU's smaller and medium-sized companies to stick to the bloc's many environment laws and to exploit their potential.

The ministers' informal meeting in Amsterdam, chaired by Dutch Environment Minister Margaretha de Boer, will look at law enforcement among such companies and ways to improve knowledge of EU directives.

Ministers' talks on Saturday morning will centre on a study defining the needs and problems of EU companies with between 20 and 100 employees. This covers the vast majority of firms in sectors such as metalworking, engineering, textiles, printing, food processing, timber and specialist chemicals.
The study identifies the main environmental threats posed by such companies as their use of water and chemicals, emissions to water and waste production.
It says smaller manufacturing firms usually lack staff with enough environmental knowledge or expertise to tackle problems or even to keep up to date on new laws.
